To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the diffusion rate of dopamine and dopamine agonists through tissue was rather slow; (2) the diffusion rate was dependent on the molecular size and lipophilicity of the compounds; (3) the diffusion of dopamine was not affected by dopamine agonists; and (4) a fast diffusion rate was observed in the case of the Na+ channel blocker, TTX, which could also be explained on the basis of remote inhibition of neurons.
we developed a dual-probe method to assess the penetration rate of drugs infused into the striatal brain tissue of rats, and that we observed a broad range of penetration rates for several compounds.

the penetration rate in brain tissue is a crucial parameter in microdialysis studies and that the dual-probe microdiaylsis technique is a suitable method for evaluation of the diffusion rate of compounds from the probe.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new microdialysis technique to evaluate the penetration of compounds through brain tissue, using a dual-probe system.
the diffusion rate of pharmacological agents in brain tissue.
the development of methods to evaluate the migration rate of drugs from the microdialysis probes into the brain tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
retrodialysis is not a reliable method for drug infusion into brain tissue.
the penetration rate depends on the compound and the experimental conditions.
the diffusion rates of drugs from a probe into the tissue are dependent upon the molecular properties of the compounds and the local environment of the probe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diffusion rate of a drug is not a simple function of the size and shape of a molecule, but also depends on the specific interaction of the drug with the tissue.
retrodialysis experiments should be interpreted carefully and that the diffusion rate should be taken into account.
the dual-probe micro dialysis technique is very useful to study the diffusion rate of compounds in the brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pharmacological effects of compounds infused into the brain by retrodialysis can be evaluated by a second microdialysis fiber positioned 1 mm away from the infusion fiber.
the penetration rate is a crucial factor in determining the concentration gradient between brain and probe.
the penetration rate should be considered when interpreting microdialysis results.
